hints: Look closely at the word metaphase. Are the 26 chromosomes in this cell made of one chromatid or two sister chromatids joined together?
Remember each single chromatid has two ends, so two telomeres. How many chromatids are present in total, and how many ends does that give?
walkthrough:
**Recall what a telomere is**

Think of a telomere as the protective cap on the end of a DNA molecule. Every chromatid has two ends, so every chromatid has two telomeres.

**Check the chromosome structure in metaphase**

In metaphase of mitosis, DNA has already been replicated in interphase. So each of the 26 chromosomes is made of two sister chromatids joined at the centromere.

Total chromatids:
$$26 \text{ chromosomes} \times 2 = 52 \text{ chromatids}$$

**Calculate total telomeres**

Now multiply chromatids by telomeres per chromatid.
$$52 \text{ chromatids} \times 2 \text{ telomeres} = 104 \text{ telomeres}$$
That is what the scientist will see glowing under the microscope.

options.A: 26 counts only one telomere per chromosome, but each chromatid has two ends and each metaphase chromosome has two chromatids.
options.B: 52 counts two telomeres per chromosome, which is correct for an unreplicated chromosome but forgets that in metaphase each chromosome has two sister chromatids.
options.C: 78 has no biological basis here and does not fit the 2 chromatids x 2 ends per chromosome pattern.
options.D: 104 is correct because 26 chromosomes x 2 chromatids x 2 telomeres per chromatid gives 104 telomeres in metaphase.
